title: Three Domains and Classification

mcqs.question: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by:
Fungi are separated from plants in the five-kingdom system because they:
The three-domain system is based on:
In bryophytes, the dominant generation is:

notes: Three-domain system (Woese, 1977): Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya — based on 16S rRNA gene sequences.
Five-kingdom classification (Whittaker, 1969): Monera (prokaryotes), Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — based on cell type and mode of nutrition.
Binomial nomenclature (Linnaeus, 1753): Genus species (italicised, e.g. Rhododendron arboreum).
Taxonomic hierarchy: Domain > Kingdom > Phylum/Division > Class > Order > Family > Genus > Species.
Plantae: eukaryotic, autotrophic, cell wall (cellulose); includes algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms, angiosperms.
Plant evolution: algae → bryophytes (non-vascular) → pteridophytes (seedless vascular) → gymnosperms (naked seeds) → angiosperms (flowers + enclosed seeds).
Alternation of generations: haploid gametophyte ↔ diploid sporophyte; in bryophytes the gametophyte is dominant; in seed plants the sporophyte is dominant.
confusion: Five-kingdom (Whittaker) separates fungi from plants; the older two-kingdom (Linnaeus) placed fungi under plants.
Three-domain and five-kingdom are complementary: domains refer to genetic/cell structure; kingdoms to ecological role.
In bryophytes, the Gametophyte (n) is the dominant, visible generation; in seed plants the Sporophyte (2n) is dominant.
Pteridophytes have true vascular tissue (xylem + phloem) but no seeds; bryophytes lack true vascular tissue.
Gymnosperms produce "naked" seeds in cones; angiosperms produce seeds enclosed in fruit.

State the key features of the three-domain classification.
Give the scientific name of three Nepali plants using binomial nomenclature.
universalFacts: Linnaeus named over 7,000 plant and animal species using binomial nomenclature.
Whittaker's five-kingdom system (1969) is still the most widely used teaching classification.
Nepal's national flower, Rhododendron arboreum, belongs to the family Rhododendraceae (order Ericales).
DNA-based phylogenetics has shown that all eukaryotes share a common ancestor distinct from prokaryotes.
examples: Rhododendron arboreum (Nepal national flower) — Division Magnoliophyta, family Rhododendraceae.
Pinus merkusii — Division Pinophyta, gymnosperm; a common Himalayan conifer.
Oryza sativa (rice) — Division Magnoliophyta, family Poaceae; staple food of Nepal.

formulas: Taxonomic hierarchy: Domain → Kingdom → Phylum/Division → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Binomial nomenclature: Genus + specific epithet (e.g., Homo sapiens)
Alternation of generations: Sporophyte (2n) → Spores (n) → Gametophyte (n) → Gametes → Zygote (2n)
keyPoints: Three domains: Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya (based on 16S rRNA).
Five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia (Whittaker, 1969).
Taxonomic hierarchy: 8 ranks from Domain to Species.
Binomial nomenclature: Genus species (italicised, two-part Latin name).
Alternation of generations: key feature of all land plants.
Plant evolution: algae → bryophytes → pteridophytes → gymnosperms → angiosperms.
enrichedContent.summary: Modern taxonomy classifies life using two complementary systems: the three-domain system (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya) based on molecular evidence, and the five-kingdom system (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) based on cell structure and nutrition. The taxonomic hierarchy (Domain → Species) and binomial nomenclature (Genus species) provide universal naming. Plant evolution shows a progressive transition from simple algae to complex angiosperms, with alternation of generations as a unifying feature.
specialNotes: NEB expects students to know the five-kingdom system (Whittaker) and the three-domain system (Woese) with their bases of classification.
Taxonomic hierarchy questions are very frequent — memorise all 8 ranks with examples.
Binomial nomenclature: always italicise or underline the full scientific name; only the genus is capitalised.
Alternation of generations is a hallmark of Plantae; the dominant generation (gametophyte vs sporophyte) varies by division.
importantStatements: The three-domain system reorganised all life into three primary lineages based on 16S rRNA sequence analysis.
Whittaker's five-kingdom system remains the most widely used classification in school-level biology.
All land plants undergo alternation of generations between haploid and diploid phases.
The evolution of the flower and seed (angiosperm innovation) made plants the most successful terrestrial group.

Practice writing scientific names: Rhododendron arboreum, Oryza sativa, Pinus merkusii.
Understand alternation of generations with a labelled cycle diagram.

Bryophyte = dominant gametophyte; seed plant = dominant sporophyte.
